instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.66 requires every person who lobbies as a lobbyist (defined in §13.62(11) as someone receiving economic consideration from a principal whose duties include lobbying) to be licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, so all paid lobbyists must register.

The lobbyist license under §13.63(1)(a) expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, and principal registration under §13.64(2) also expires on December 31 of each even-numbered year, making the renewal cycle biennial (24 months).

Section 13.695(2) requires that any change in name or general area of legislative action be reported in writing to the board within 10 days of the change; this is the closest statutory change-notification deadline in the bundle (note: §13.695 governs agency filings; no separate change-of-registration deadline is set for private lobbyists).

Section 13.66 forbids any person from engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless already licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65, and §13.65 requires the authorization to be filed "before engaging in lobbying," meaning the lobbyist must register before any lobbying activity (0 days after).

The lobbyist must obtain a separate license under §13.63(1)(a), the principal must file a separate registration statement under §13.64(1), and a separate authorization linking the two must be filed under §13.65 — three distinct filings rather than a single combined form.
Section 13.63(1) specifies the contents of a lobbyist license application (signature, social security number, fee) and does not require submission of a photograph.
Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees acting in an official capacity from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, and 13.695.

Section 13.621(2) provides that a state agency that files a statement under §13.695 (and officials named in it) are not subject to §§13.625, 13.63, 13.64, 13.65, or 13.68, substituting a separate, lighter agency-specific reporting regime under §13.695.
